header:
Date: 2025-12-22
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Aurora CTO), Sofia Martinez (Aurora ML), Tom Reeves (Aurora DevOps)
summary: Discovery focused on Dedicated (reserved GPUs) for Aurora Tech's inference workloads. Key topics: isolation requirements (VPC, data residency), burst/burst-to-hosted strategy, scaling expectations for Q1, perf targets (tail latency), and compliance needs (SOC2/KMS). Agreed to run pilot benchmarks and share pricing/contract draft.
topics: Current infra and constraints; workload profile (models, sequence length, qps); isolation and data controls; burst strategy and fallback to hosted; scaling and autoscaling policies; benchmarks and SLAs; next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm maya from redwood, liam is our systems engineer.
[00:12] Raj Patel: Hi, Raj here. CTO at Aurora. we run recommendation models and a document Q&A product.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: Sofia, ML eng — mostly model infra and perf.
[00:25] Tom Reeves: Tom, DevOps, i'll own the network side.
[00:33] Liam O'Connor: Quick agenda: understand current infra, why dedicated, isolation needs, burst pattern, perf goals, and next steps.
[01:05] Raj Patel: Why dedicated? we need predictable throughput and full isolation for some regulated customers. also lower unit cost vs hosted at our scale.
[01:22] Maya Chen: Makes sense. can you describe current traffic and models? qps, typical sequence lengths, peak windows?
[01:35] Sofia Martinez: We have two main models: a 13B chat-style model for Q&A (avg seq len 250 tokens) and a smaller 2.7B for reranking. Baseline 50 qps, peaks to 350 qps for short bursts, mostly weekday mornings. GPU fleet currently mixed p4/ a100 in cloud.
[01:58] Tom Reeves: Our infra is in GCP us-central with VPC peering to internal services. some compliance customers require private networking and key separation.
[02:16] Liam O'Connor: For dedicated, we usually propose reserved GPU pools. do you have a target for reserved vs burst-to-hosted?
[02:28] Raj Patel: Want to reserve for baseline and burst to hosted for big spikes — but need guarantees on cold-start and latency when bursting.
[02:40] Maya Chen: Right, we can do reserved capacity for steady throughput and configured burst capacity for overflow to Redwood hosted or Dedicated on-demand. there are options for fast warmers and prewarmed KV cache priming to reduce cold-starts.
[02:58] Sofia Martinez: how do you handle state — like KV caches for chat? if we route to hosted during bursts, will the KV cache be lost?
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: Good question. by default KV cache is local to the serving pool. we support prefix caching and optional shared cache layers in Dedicated if you want consistent latency across pools, but shared caches have tradeoffs. when bursting to hosted, you can expect slightly higher latencies until caches are primed; we can prewarm using traffic mirroring for the pilot.
[03:41] Raj Patel: ok, what's the sizing recommendation? we currently see median latency 120ms token for the 13B. want p95 under 400ms at peak.
[03:55] Liam O'Connor: For 13B and those sequence lengths, p95 under 400ms at 350 qps will need roughly 4x A100 equivalent GPUs with concurrent request multiplexing depending on batching. for cost predictability we typically recommend reserving the equivalent of 3-4 GPUs for baseline with burst headroom.
[04:22] Tom Reeves: Are these exclusive GPUs or multi-tenant? we need strict isolation for a subset of clients.
[04:30] Maya Chen: Dedicated offers isolated GPU pools — physical isolation per tenant or logical isolation depending on contract. for regulated customers we do single-tenant nodes and VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed networking.
[04:44] Raj Patel: Great. security: SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS integration, audit logs — we will need those artifacts.
[04:54] Maya Chen: We'll share SOC2 report, network diagrams and our KMS/HSM integration notes. we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated in enterprise plans.
[05:06] Sofia Martinez: What about quantization and perf tradeoffs? we often use int8 to reduce cost but worried about quality regressions for the Q&A model.
[05:18] Liam O'Connor: We can provide quantization profiles per model — Redwood Optimize suggests profiles and we run evals against your prompt set to track regressions. for initial pilot we recommend FP16 on A100 then evaluate int8 if quality tolerates it.
[05:36] Raj Patel: Burst pattern again: we need <2s cold-start for model containers when scaling up or switching to hosted. possible?
[05:45] Liam O'Connor: With prewarmed workers and rapid scaling policies, we can target sub-2s for container readiness, but KV cache priming might add token-level latency until warmed. we also offer warm standby instances for critical endpoints to keep tail latency low.
[06:05] Tom Reeves: Network egress and VPC — if we keep control plane private, how do we handle updates and telemetry?
[06:14] Maya Chen: We can set up a private control plane with peered endpoints; telemetry can be forwarded to your logging account via secure collectors. for on-prem we provide an air-gapped option for regulated workloads.
[06:28] Raj Patel: SLA expectations? what uptime and latency guarantees do you offer on Dedicated?
[06:35] Liam O'Connor: Dedicated plans come with SLA tiers — typical is 99.9% uptime with latency SLOs for model families; specifics are in the SLA appendix. for pilots we usually run without SLA then move to contractual SLA after commit.
[06:52] Sofia Martinez: Any gating items for pilot? what do you need from us to run benchmark?
[06:58] Liam O'Connor: We'll need representative workload (prompts), a target perf matrix (qps, seq len, p95 target), network egress estimates, and temporary API credentials or request replay dataset. we'll run A/B tests across model variants and quantization settings.
[07:20] Raj Patel: Cost question: what's the delta between reserved and hosted per token?
[07:27] Maya Chen: Reserved typically lowers unit cost significantly; exact delta depends on commit size and GPU type. i'll send a pricing sheet, but rough ballpark: reserved A100-backed capacity can be 30-50% lower per-token vs pure hosted at scale.
[07:45] Sofia Martinez: Are there any limits on canary/rollouts? we run frequent model updates.
[07:52] Liam O'Connor: Redwood supports canary rollouts, traffic-splitting, and automatic fallback policies. Dedicated customers can configure per-route rollouts tied to model versions.
[08:05] Tom Reeves: We need RBAC + SSO. supported?
[08:10] Maya Chen: Yes, SAML/SSO, SCIM, RBAC roles, and audit logs are available. we'll include examples in the security packet.
[08:20] Raj Patel: Curious about monitoring — token-level cost, per-model latency breakouts?
[08:26] Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency, and traces. we can also stream raw telemetry to your prometheus/grafana.
[08:40] Sofia Martinez: If we choose dedicated with reserved capacity, any recommended autoscaling policy?
[08:46] Liam O'Connor: We recommend baseline reserved capacity sized for sustained qps and a burst policy that steps up by 1-2x using on-demand pools; for unpredictable spikes use hosted fallback. also intelligent batching and TTL-based KV cache reduce pressure.
[09:05] Raj Patel: How long to provision dedicated pool?
[09:09] Maya Chen: Provisioning depends on region and GPU availability — typically 2-6 weeks for reserved pools; we can accelerate for priority customers if needed.
[09:19] Tom Reeves: Billing model for dedicated? monthly commit? upfront?
[09:24] Maya Chen: Typically monthly or annual reserved commits. billing for burst usage can be pay-as-you-go or capped depending on contract.
[09:35] Sofia Martinez: Are there known noisy-neighbor protections if we do multi-tenant?
[09:41] Liam O'Connor: Yes, the runtime has cgroup isolation, per-tenant scheduling, and kernel tuning to avoid noisy neighbor effects; still for strict compliance we recommend single-tenant nodes.
[09:58] Raj Patel: Any integration work for our infra team?
[10:02] Tom Reeves: we'll need terraform modules, network peering, and IAM setup.
[10:10] Maya Chen: We provide terraform modules, runbooks, and a solutions enablement packet.
[10:18] Sofia Martinez: For pilot, let's run two scenarios: baseline reserved 3 A100 equiv + burst to hosted; and 4 A100 equiv reserved for peak. compare cost and latency.
[10:28] Liam O'Connor: Perfect; we'll propose a benchmark plan.
[10:32] Raj Patel: Any gotchas around data residency? some contracts require EU-only processing.
[10:38] Maya Chen: Dedicated can be constrained to region; Private deployment is the path for strict residency or on-prem. we'll flag options in the security packet.
[10:49] Tom Reeves: One more — do you support customer-managed KMS for encryption keys?
[10:54] Maya Chen: Yes for Dedicated and Private. we support customer KMS via HSM integrations.
[11:05] Raj Patel: Okay let's recap next steps.
[11:08] Maya Chen: Recap — maya sends pricing and contract; liam sends benchmark plan; tom provides utilization numbers; raj confirms stakeholders for security review. schedule pilot next week.
[11:20] Raj Patel: Sounds good. thanks all.
[11:24] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links: pricing deck, SOC2, network diagram, and perf spreadsheet.
[11:30] (call ends)
closing_notes: Call ended with pilot agreed; action items assigned. transcription contains some imperfect ASR of technical terms (e.g., model sizes and GPU types).
